# Jubilees Chapter 32 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Back to Bethel; Levi ordained; seven heavenly tablets

---

**32:1** That night at Bethel, an angel of the LORD came to Jacob: "I am the God of Bethel — where you set up the stone and made your vow. It's time to leave this place and go back home."

**32:2** Jacob was up before dawn, gathered everyone — wives, children, everything they owned — and headed for Bethel.

**32:3** At Bethel he made burnt offerings on the altar he had built years before, and he gave God a tenth of everything he had brought with him.

**32:4** Around this same time, Levi had a dream. In the dream, God's angels came down from heaven and set him apart to be a priest — to stand and serve before the LORD.

**32:5** Jacob woke from his own sleep that night and praised God.

**32:6** Jacob counted his sons: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulun, Joseph, Benjamin. Twelve sons.

**32:7** He counted again — and on the second count, the tenth position fell to Levi. That was the lot: Levi was the tithe.

**32:8** In the middle of the night, Jacob got up and consecrated Levi — dressed him in clean clothes and anointed him with sacred oil.

**32:9** And right there at the gate of Bethel, Jacob set aside ten animals from his herd as the LORD's tithe.

**32:10** In the morning he sat down with Levi and walked him through everything required of a priest, and formally commissioned him to serve before the LORD.

**32:11** The LORD appeared to Jacob again at Bethel and blessed him: "From now on your name is not Jacob — it's Israel."

**32:12** "I am the LORD your God, maker of heaven and earth. I will make you grow and multiply. Kings will come from your line, and they will govern all humanity.

**32:13** Your descendants will inherit every land under heaven. They will rule the nations as they see fit, and in the end they will take possession of the whole earth."

**32:14** Then God finished speaking and ascended. Jacob stood watching until he was gone.

**32:15** That same night, in a vision, Jacob saw an angel come down from heaven carrying seven tablets. The angel handed them to Jacob. Jacob read every word — the full history of what would happen to him and his children down through all the ages.

**32:16** He brought the tablets to his father Isaac and showed them to him that night. Isaac read them and wept: "Everything written here will come true for your descendants."

**32:17** But through the tears, Isaac was joyful — because the vision showed that Jacob's descendants would be great. He gave Jacob a final blessing and went to sleep.

**32:18** Jacob went to Rachel, who was pregnant. He wrote everything down — all the visions, all the words.

**32:19** During this period, the Canaanite tribes of the region began threatening Jacob and his household.

**32:20** But nothing came of it. God had put a fear of Jacob into all the surrounding nations, and they kept their distance. Jacob was never harmed.

**32:21** That same year, Laban — Jacob's father-in-law — died. Jacob now had twelve sons.

**32:22** Rachel gave birth to her second son. Jacob named him Benjamin — "son of his old age," is what the name means.

---

*PNEUMA notes: The designation of Levi as the "tithe" (tenth lot) in vv.6-7 is a clever narrative device in Jubilees connecting the Levitical tithe to the patriarchal count. The seven tablets (v.15) are a unique vision giving Jubilees' author authority for his expanded retelling. The second name-change at Bethel (v.11) parallels Genesis 35:10.*
